about: The tillr backend policy for a machine whose only provider is Amazon Bedrock (the work profile). Same shape and same rules as backend-policy.json beside it, which is the personal machines' policy; a drain on a Bedrock machine names this file with --policy. The build seat runs Terra and the scout seat runs Luna (the owner's instruction of 2026-11-18, to put cheaper models on implementation and scouting); the review seat runs the profile's workhorse row, Sol 6.2 (back on 2026-11-18 once the early-quit cause was found in the brief and fixed) and the design seat runs the frontier row. An item that names no seat (an ordinary single-worker item) takes default_backend, so that is Terra too, with Sol 6.2 as its failover; the review seat is named explicitly and stays on Sol 6.2. All go through the pi adapter. Two files is the stopgap docs/design/tillr-convergence.md OQ-TC2 records: the target is that tillr names only seats and the machine's profile resolves them, at which point this file is deleted.
